translationRepairs: On his mother's side his great-grandfather was Xin Wu-xian, General Who Subdues the Qiang, celebrated for strategic daring.
On his mother's side his high ancestor (maternal great-great-grandfather) was Xin Wuxian, General Who Subdues the Qiang, celebrated for strategic daring.
外高祖 is the maternal high ancestor (great-great-grandfather, fourth ascending generation), not great-grandfather (外曾祖); the repair also normalizes Xin Wuxian.
Yongyuan 1 saw Dou Xian, Grand General, recall Fu Yi as chief clerk and name Cui Yin registrar.
Yongyuan 1 saw Dou Xian, General of Chariots and Cavalry, recall Fu Yi as chief clerk and name Cui Yin registrar.
s0194 titles Dou 车骑将军; 大将军 appears only later in s0195 when he is promoted, so Grand General is wrong here.
In the first Yongyuan year Grand General Dou Xian again named Yi chief secretary and Cui Yin registrar.
In the first Yongyuan year General of Chariots and Cavalry Dou Xian again named Yi chief secretary and Cui Yin registrar.
Literal line must match 车骑将军 as General of Chariots and Cavalry; Grand General conflates with the later 大将军 promotion.
Cui Qi, styled Ziwei, from Anping in Zhuo, shared descent with Jinbei chancellor Cui Yuan.
Cui Qi, styled Ziwei, from Anping in Zhuo, shared descent with Jibei chancellor Cui Yuan.
濟北相 is Chancellor of Jibei; Jinbei misreads 济/濟 as Jin.
Cui Qi, courtesy name Ziwei, was a man of Anping in Zhuo commandery, of the same lineage as Chancellor of Jinbei Cui Yuan.
Cui Qi, courtesy name Ziwei, was a man of Anping in Zhuo commandery, of the same lineage as Chancellor of Jibei Cui Yuan.
Literal Jinbei likewise errs; 濟北 is Jibei, matching the idiomatic repair.
In Yongchu of Emperor An, recommended filial and incorrupt; served as Privy Treasurer aide; submitted four convenient proposals; appointed magistrate of Tangyin.
In Yongchu of Emperor An, recommended filial and incorrupt; served as Grand Provisioner aide; submitted four convenient proposals; appointed magistrate of Tangyin.
太官丞 is Grand Provisioner aide (imperial kitchen), not Privy Treasurer (少府); the idiomatic line already has the kitchen sense.
